method: Targeted runtime entry-point, import, flag and consumer inspection. Static evidence proves implementation; no production execution or learning effectiveness verified. No application tests or providers invoked.
unknowns: Production flags, database agent records, usage telemetry, deployed content coverage, live student outcomes, real-device accessibility and offline reliability remain unverified.

evidence.claim: The executable published ontology registry contains only Grade 4 Math; other grades/subjects do not receive a governed release by inference.
Authenticated server entry resolves published release, persists decisions, seals diagnostic sessions and server scores answers.
Canonical state reads require learner membership; writes validate governed evidence identity and released bindings rather than trusting client mastery.
Versioned mastery reducer models confidence, retention and misconception state; this is an implemented state model, not proof of educational validity.
Default ranking is deterministic and considers evidence sufficiency/conflicts/retention. It is not an LLM agent.
Early personalization mixes are explicitly a STARTING_HYPOTHESIS_REQUIRES_EDUCATIONAL_REVIEW, not validated outcomes.
AI_TUTOR_ENABLED and Edge Config both gate tutor; STUDENT role, rate limit and server-resolved context precede generation.
Student tutor is a compatibility adapter to the shared groundedAnswerService, so counting it as an independent orchestration engine would double count.
Grounded answer generation moderates input/output, uses a bounded regeneration, validates citations, handles weak grounding and budget block, and tells the model sources are untrusted.
Tutor context rejects assessment content and recognizable protected answer/teacher fields. Regex checks alone are not a general prompt-injection proof.

Eight role stages run injected executors in fixed dependencies, bounded attempts 1-5, hash-linked events and self-review checks. The workflow lacks approval/official writers and ends awaiting human review.
Exact source hash and DRAFT/PENDING runtime binding preserve first-three authoring provenance; returned bindings remain studentEligible:false, approved:false, released:false.
Four persisted AI review identities use router/configured-provider and prompt fingerprints, minimum confidence 70, provisioned enabled:false unless explicitly enabled.
Flag-gated platform-admin route requires idempotency key then provisions review agents with enable:true. Changing gate can activate records on invocation; not purely a read flag.
Subject/pedagogy reviewers run, optional WAEC and disagreement adjudicator follow. CRITICAL tasks blocked, stale revisions rejected, final result advisory only with required audit.
V2 consumers are pure readers and downstream writes are hardcoded false. This architecture is deliberately not an activated official record pipeline.
Learner allow-list projection keeps protected scoring fields out; independent delivery cannot be downgraded and hint access is blocked.
Documented V2 omissions include persistence, API routes, player UI and moderation queue. Existing runtime adopts selected safe adapters and candidate review, not full production V2 lifecycle.
7/21-day retention policy and opportunity planner exist; policy comments explicitly say scheduler, delivery and evidence writes are not wired.
Official grades reject raw/provisional/unofficial/revoked/unauthorized scores; assisted or unknown independence requires moderation rather than automatic official points.
Legacy classifier distinguishes teacher approval/regrading from AI auto-release/unmoderated suggestions.
Teacher gradebook reader exposes official score/feedback only for classifier result TEACHER.
Student assignment reader suppresses score unless classifier result TEACHER.
Report card generation skips submissions without TEACHER score authority.
Learning success requires unassisted matched learners, retained/transfer gain and independent comparable evidence; delivery/completion alone never demonstrates learning success.
Current AI placement issuance is hardcoded mathematics with server fallback bank. No multi-subject calibrated diagnostic coverage or psychometric reliability evidence established.
Academic enrollment input accepts grades 1-12, which does not provide a Kindergarten grade path.
Supported request locales are en, kpe and bss; Koloqua is absent from this executable locale registry.
Visible language options are English, Kpelle, Bassa; absence of Koloqua corroborates locale registry gap.
AI suggestedScore is stored as LabSession.score and sent to StudentPerformanceEvent with aiAssistUsed:false. This establishes scoring provenance ambiguity, not a proven official-grade write.
Moderation fallback has suggestedScore zero, so fallback can look like actual low performance to the completion writer.
Performance event persistence feeds confusion detection by queue or direct scheduler, making advisory scoring provenance operationally consequential.
Without an explicit governed mapping, lab events remain RAW_OBSERVATION or PROVISIONAL; only approved published mapped evidence can become canonical.
AI lab planner is default-off flag-gated, STUDENT-authenticated and rate-limited; returned proposed actions run deterministic validateLabAction.
AI lab explainer is flag/role-gated but unlike planner route lacks route-level checkAiRateLimit. Central provider budget is not a per-user throttle.
One endpoint has a weekly-class planning branch using lib/teacher/lessonPlanner while its other branch uses lib/ai/teacher/lessonPlanner; overlapping planning families should share contracts.
Moderation-blocked grading returns synthetic grade 50 with teacher-review message, so callers must never treat all returned numeric grades as achieved performance.
Tutor and teacher assist default off. Additional reviewed flag sections show adaptive/intervention/planning/grading defaults on, virtual labs/AI labs default off. Production values unknown.

Submitted IDs are fetched globally without issued-session, subject or grade binding. Replays and duplicate IDs are not rejected before updateMasteryProfile records unassisted legacy mastery. This is not evidence of canonical SLM mutation.
GET may generate missing practice bank content; POST has no issued attempt/idempotency and chooses first enrollment school. No route AI request throttling is present.
LLM-generated questions pass moderation and shape checks then enter practice bank directly, outside Content Factory/independent academic review. Each underfilled topic can trigger a provider call.

Existing curriculum upgrade loads persisted source lesson and drafts enriched content. Separate generator has bounded generation/repair call paths with 10000-14000 output token limits earlier in module.

Output must label AI_ASSESSED_ALIGNMENT with externalApprovalClaimed:false, and definite depth/direct alignment needs topic-level WAEC evidence.
Quiz generation and gap analysis are separate functions in one lesson assessment service, invoked from learner quiz routes. This is an on-demand service, not a scheduled autonomous agent.

Requires exactly five responses, binds sealed session to user/lesson/quiz and exact question set, and supports clientAttemptId idempotent replay.
Explicitly rejects placeholder question/Option A-D fallback content; no fabricated quiz accepted on this path was established.

recommendations.action: Keep virtual lab activation gated until AI score provenance and refusal handling are repaired
recommendations.benefit: Avoid treating safety refusal or suggested AI marks as learner failure
recommendations.acceptance: Moderation fallback creates pending review without numeric attainment; AI score stored as provisional; performance detector receives explicit scorer/provenance and excludes unverified marks; regression tests cover unsafe input and repeat submission.

recommendations.action: Deliver one approved assessment V2 persistence-to-moderation-to-official-reader vertical slice before expanding official writes
recommendations.benefit: Defensible grades and independent assessment evidence
recommendations.acceptance: One class can attempt a released form; protected fields stay server-side; retries idempotent; assistance disqualifies independence; second marking and revocation propagate; teacher publishes final records; downstream write constant remains unchanged until explicit authorization.

recommendations.action: Publish one complete coherent schoolday pilot with explicit curriculum coverage and governance ledger
recommendations.benefit: Students and teachers can complete a real school day using approved materials
recommendations.owner: Chief of Staff + Content Factory + interactive learning
recommendations.acceptance: Every scheduled period has approved released lesson/activity/assessment, teacher materials and offline fallback; dry-run shows no draft or unsupported launch; coverage gaps visible rather than substituted silently.

recommendations.action: Expand governed releases one subject/grade unit at a time using existing learning state/orchestrator
recommendations.benefit: Persistent learning profiles and trustworthy remediation beyond Grade 4 Math
recommendations.acceptance: Next scope has reviewed prerequisite graph, independent diagnostic items, scored bindings and misconception policies; unsupported scope returns explicit gaps; replay/tenant/idempotency tests pass.

recommendations.action: Run measured pilot before claiming instructional effectiveness
recommendations.benefit: Decisions based on retained understanding and transfer rather than engagement
recommendations.acceptance: Pre-register baseline/post/delayed/transfer measures, retain revision/learner linkage and comparison assumptions; report uncertainty and exclusions with classifyLessonOutcome; no claim of demonstrated success from completion counts.

recommendations.action: Wire a controlled 7/21-day retention workflow for an approved unit
recommendations.benefit: Detect forgetting and assign verified retrieval practice
recommendations.acceptance: One learner receives due opportunities exactly once, with independent/no-tutor status, missed-day handling, offline capture and teacher visibility; due state does not itself imply lost mastery.

recommendations.action: Define Kindergarten and Koloqua pilot contracts
recommendations.benefit: Close explicit founder vision exclusions without pretending Kpelle/Bassa provide Koloqua
recommendations.acceptance: Kindergarten enrollment/curriculum/reporting flows have explicit grade-band policy; Koloqua reviewed sample module, language preference and English equivalent preserve meaning and assessment validity.

recommendations.action: Consolidate teacher planner/grading contracts while preserving useful task modes
recommendations.benefit: Fewer divergent prompt, moderation and provenance policies
recommendations.acceptance: All current callers use one versioned planner contract and one advisory grading contract with task mode; same limits/provenance, no endpoint removed until callers migrate and parity verified.

recommendations.action: Bind WAEC practice marking to a server-issued immutable attempt before admitting mastery
recommendations.benefit: Prevent replay, duplicate answers and arbitrary-item evidence from inflating legacy learner profiles
recommendations.acceptance: Server-issued attempt pins student, school, subject, grade and question IDs; scoring exactly once rejects duplicates/unissued/cross-subject IDs and replay; assistance provenance retained; question generation requires rate/budget bounds and reviewed provisional content status.
